subject: Prod queueing & reserved throughput degradation - exec intervention requested
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@skybridge-payments.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production slowdown - queues and 95th latency spike

Camila,

Heads up — starting ~08:45 PDT we're seeing a sustained spike in model response times for our production route (route_id: skybridge-pay). 95th pct latency climbed from ~230ms to 2.4s and token error rates rose from ~0.2% to ~3.7%. Throughput is throttled even though our reserved capacity shows a 30% allocation. Several customer-facing flows are timing out.

Attached is a short CSV from our telemetry ingest and a screenshot of the Redwood console showing queue depth. We're running on the dedicated GPU pool you quoted (dedicated-pool-us-west-2-a). This is affecting settlement and risk scoring — high business impact.

Can you confirm what immediate mitigations you can do? We need an ETA for remediation. If there's an SRE/exec you want on the call, escalate please.

Marco Ruiz
Head of Platform
Skybridge Payments

Marco — thanks for the flag and the attachments. We're escalating to SRE and CS leads and standing up a bridge now. Early read from our telemetry: reserved-pool headroom is reporting 12% free, while queue depth on the route shows sustained tail growth consistent with a bursty workload pattern.

Immediate actions we are taking (will update on the bridge):
- Opening a live bridge with SRE (Rishi) and CS (Naomi) — link incoming.
- Temporarily relaxing autoscaler policy for dedicated-pool-us-west-2-a to allow short-term hot add of instances (30min window) to relieve queueing.
- Enabling model fallback to a lower-latency quantized variant for non-critical settlement calls to reduce token work.

I know this is urgent — I'm looping Naomi for customer comms and Rishi for technical remediation. We'll aim to have visible improvement within the hour and a proposed remediation plan within 2 hours.

Cc'ing Marissa for visibility.

—Camila

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production slowdown - queues and 95th latency spike

Team — summary of what SRE has observed after initial triage:

Observations:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-us-west-2-a) shows 78% GPU utilization averaged across nodes, but sustained request queue depth for skybridge-pay route increased sharply at 08:40 PDT concurrent with an internal batch job spike from another tenant within the same pool.
- KV cache hit rates for the model fell from 94% -> 67% as sequence lengths increased (likely longer prompts from batch job). That increased effective token-work per request and exacerbated queueing.
- Error rates correlate to token timeouts when queueing pushed effective token processing beyond per-request timeouts.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Temporarily increased per-pool headroom by hot-adding two instances (manual hot-add) and relaxed autoscaler thresholds for the next 45 minutes. Visible queue depth reduced by ~60% within 12 minutes.
- Enabled route-level model fallback: non-critical settlement endpoints are now served by model-redwood-q8-medium (quantized) until capacity stabilizes.
- Blacklisted the identified batch job owner from the shared pool pending further coordination; will propose a migration to isolated reserved lanes to prevent recurrence.

Next steps / ask for execs:
- Recommend a short-term capacity reserve for Skybridge (additional 1 GPU-equivalent) for 30 days while we migrate noisy tenants to separate lanes — requires approval from Sales/Finance to bill as an out-of-band effort or apply a billing credit.
- Schedule a cross-functional postmortem and a permanent plan to provide lane isolation for high-throughput customers (INF-3492).

I've attached a short runbook for temporary bump and rollback. If Sales/Finance approves, we can formalize the temporary reservation immediately.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
